description: Run, restore, convert and preview .NET 10+ file-based apps (single .cs files), with language-tagged comment rendering for /*markdown, /*yaml, /*json and more.
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: Running, building, publishing or converting file-based apps executes the .NET SDK and is disabled in Restricted Mode. Tagged-comment highlighting, hover and preview remain available.
capabilities.virtualWorkspaces.descripti: File-based app commands require a local or remote file system with the .NET SDK.
command.enableForFile: Enable File Apps Toolkit for This File
command.disableForFile: Disable File Apps Toolkit for This File
configuration.title: .NET File Apps Toolkit
config.enabled: Show toolkit commands and editor actions for .NET file-based apps.
config.fileDetection: How `.cs` files are recognized as file-based apps. Files can always be opted in or out with **Enable/Disable File Apps Toolkit for This File**.
config.fileDetection.strict: Only files that start with `#:` directives (`#:package`, `#:sdk`, …) or a `dotnet` shebang.
config.fileDetection.standalone: Also files with top-level statements that are not inside a project (`.csproj`) directory tree.
config.fileDetection.manual: Only files explicitly enabled with the Enable command.
config.dotnetPath: Path to the `dotnet` executable used on the extension host. Can only be set in user (machine) settings.
config.autoSaveBeforeRun: What to do when the file has unsaved changes before running a .NET CLI command.
config.autoSaveBeforeRun.never: Never save; the command is blocked while the file has unsaved changes.
config.run.args: Default application arguments for **Run File**. Each array item is passed as one argument (no shell parsing).
config.comments.enabled: Recognize explicitly language-tagged block comments such as `/*markdown`, `/*yaml` and `/*json` (hover, decorations, preview).
config.comments.highlight.enabled: Enable color decorations inside tagged code comments (`/*yaml`, `/*json`, ...) and emphasis decorations inside `/*markdown` comments. The static TextMate injection grammar is applied by VS Code and stays active regardless of this setting.
config.comments.highlight.strategy: How tagged comment bodies are highlighted in the C# editor. A TextMate injection grammar always provides scopes; C# semantic highlighting (C# extension, C# Dev Kit) paints comment colors over them, so decorations can restore the colors.
config.comments.highlight.strategy.auto: Use the injection grammar, and add color decorations when a C# semantic tokens provider is present or a C# extension is installed. High contrast themes and disabled semantic highlighting use the injection grammar only.
config.comments.highlight.strategy.injec: Use only the injection grammar. With C# semantic highlighting active, tagged bodies may appear in the plain comment color.
config.comments.highlight.strategy.decor: Always paint the bundled highlighter's Light+/Dark+ colors over tagged code bodies.
config.comments.highlight.strategy.off: No color or Markdown decorations. The injection grammar still applies (see README).
config.comments.markdown.hover: Show a rendered Markdown hover for `/*markdown` comments.
config.comments.previewOnOpen: Automatically open the tagged comment preview beside C# files that contain tagged comments.
config.comments.unknownTagDiagnostic: Report an information diagnostic for block comments that look like `/*tag` with an unknown language.
config.comments.validation.enabled: Opt in to syntax validation for tagged YAML/JSON comments and an expandable, type-only structure preview. Disabled by default.
